rationale: This contract has a reasonable liability cap ($120,000) and mutual termination rights, making it less dangerous than a 10/10 contract. However, the HIPAA compliance disconnect is extremely problematic - the scope requires HIPAA compliance but Developer disclaims all responsibility for it. The $40,000 non-refundable deposit, unlimited scope changes at $300/hour, 180-day warranty, and no app store approval guarantee create significant financial risk. The technical complexity (dual native platforms, wearables, health data, social features) makes the 6-month timeline unrealistic. With proper negotiations, this could become acceptable.
required_changes_to_accept: Clarify HIPAA responsibilities - either Developer warrants compliance and charges appropriately, or remove HIPAA requirement from scope
Reduce non-refundable deposit to 20% ($24,000) or make partially refundable
Cap expense reimbursements at $20,000 with Client pre-approval for amounts above $5,000
Establish formal change order process requiring mutual agreement and budget adjustments
Cap additional work at $50,000 beyond original scope
Reduce warranty period to 90 days for mobile apps due to frequent OS updates
Add provisions for app store rejections - Developer makes 2 good-faith attempts, then Client can hire others
Exclude third-party API/platform changes from warranty obligations
Add realistic timeline buffer (8-9 months instead of 6)
Define 'material defects' and 'substantially conform' more precisely
Add mutual indemnification for security breaches based on fault
Clarify that wearable device integration is best-effort due to third-party dependencies
deal_breakers: If Client refuses to clarify HIPAA responsibility allocation
If Client insists on unlimited scope changes without budget adjustments
If expense reimbursements cannot be capped
